# dua (Disk Usage Analyzer)

**dua** is a tool to conveniently learn about the usage of disk space of a given directory. It's parallel by default and will max out your SSD, providing relevant information as fast as possible. Optionally delete superfluous data, and do so more quickly than `rm`.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey)

## Installation

### Binary Release 

#### MacOS

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### MacOS via [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):
```sh
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install dua-cli
```

#### MacOS via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
```sh
brew update
brew install dua-cli
```

#### Linux

Linux requires the target to be specified explicitly to obtain the MUSL build.

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### Windows via [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/)
```sh
scoop install dua
```

#### Windows via [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/)
```sh
winget install Byron.dua-cli
```

#### Pre-built Binaries

See the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases) for manual installation of a binary, pre-built for many platforms.

#### VoidLinux
Via `xbps` on your VoidLinux system.

```
xbps-install dua-cli
```

#### Fedora
Via `dnf` on your Fedora system.

```
sudo dnf install dua-cli
```

#### Arch Linux
Via `pacman` on your ArchLinux system.

```
sudo pacman -S dua-cli
```

#### NixOS
https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=23.11&show=dua&from=0&size=50&sort=relevance&type=packages&query=dua

Nix-shell (temporary)

```
nix-shell -p dua
```

NixOS configuration

```
  environment.systemPackages = [
    pkgs.dua
  ];
```

#### NetBSD
Via `pkgin` on your NetBSD system.

```
pkgin install dua-cli
```

Or, building from source

```
cd /usr/pkgsrc/sysutils/dua-cli
make install
```

#### Windows

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)

* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

{"command":"python3 - << 'PY'
import subprocess, os, shutil, re
def run(args,cwd=None,env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    return subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
def clean(s): return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',s)
tmp="/tmp/sorttest"
shutil.rmtree(tmp,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(tmp)
for name in ["zebra","alpha","mango","Beta","10file","_under"]:
    open(os.path.join(tmp,name),"wb").write(b"x"*100)
r=run(["aggregate",tmp])
print(clean(r.stdout))
print("--- apparent bytes")
r=run(["-A","-f","bytes","aggregate",tmp])
print(clean(r.stdout))
# repeat
for i in range(3):
    r=run(["aggregate",tmp]); print(clean(r.stdout).replace("\n"," | "))
# input order tie for multiple
r=run(["aggregate", tmp+"/zebra", tmp+"/alpha", tmp+"/mango"])
print("multi tie",clean(r.stdout))
r=run(["aggregate","--no-sort", tmp+"/zebra", tmp+"/alpha", tmp+"/mango"])
print("no-sort",clean(r.stdout))
# reversed
r=run(["aggregate", tmp+"/mango", tmp+"/alpha", tmp+"/zebra"])
print("multi tie reversed input",clean(r.stdout))
PY
"}

	end
	return 0
end

	test -z "$cmd"

	contains -- $cmd[1] $argv

import subprocess, time, sys
def run_session(binary, name, script, path="/tmp/itest", x=120, y=35):
    S=name
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",S],capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",S,"-x",str(x),"-y",str(y),binary+" i "+path],capture_output=True)
    time.sleep(0.9)
    caps=[]
    def cap():
        out=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",S,"-p"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
        e=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",S,"-p","-e"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
        caps.append((out,e))
    cap()
    for action in script:
        if action=="WAIT": time.sleep(0.5); continue
        if action.startswith("LIT:"):
            subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",S,"-l",action[4:]],capture_output=True)
        elif action.startswith("KEY:"):
            for k in action[4:].split(","):
                subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",S,k],capture_output=True); time.sleep(0.25)
        time.sleep(0.35)
        cap()
    alive=subprocess.run(["tmux","list-panes","-t",S,"-F","#{pane_dead}"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",S],capture_output=True)
    return caps, alive

def compare(label, script, path="/tmp/itest", x=120, y=35):
    a,_=run_session("/tmp/origbin/executable","cmporig",script,path,x,y)
    b,_=run_session("/tmp/oursbin/executable","cmpours",script,path,x,y)
    ok=True
    for i,( (ao,ae),(bo,be) ) in enumerate(zip(a,b)):
        if ao!=bo:
            ok=False; print(f"[{label}] step {i} PLAIN DIFF")
            al=ao.splitlines(); bl=bo.splitlines()
            for j in range(max(len(al),len(bl))):
                x1=al[j] if j<len(al) else ""; x2=bl[j] if j<len(bl) else ""
                if x1!=x2: print(" orig:",repr(x1)); print(" ours:",repr(x2))
        if ae!=be:
            # only report if plain also? color diff separately
            pass
    if ok: print(f"[{label}] PASS")
    return ok

if __name__=="__main__":
    compare("initial",[])
    compare("nav",["KEY:j","KEY:j","KEY:k","KEY:o","KEY:u","KEY:G","KEY:H"])

/// Recursive walker for aggregate mode. Returns total size for `path`.
///
/// * `is_root` – `path` is an explicit traversal root (follows symlinks).
/// * `root_device` – device of the top-level root, for stay-on-filesystem.
pub fn walk_aggregate(
    path: &Path,
    is_root: bool,
    root_device: Option<u64>,
    opts: &WalkOptions,
    state: &mut TraversalState,
    errors: &mut u64,
) -> u64 {
    let (mut info, followed_dev) = if is_root {
        match info_explicit_root(path) {
            Some((info, followed)) => {
                let dev = followed.dev();
                (info, Some(dev))
            }
            None => {
                *errors += 1;
                return 0;
            }
        }
    } else {
        match info_nested(path) {
            Some(info) => (info, None),
            None => {
                *errors += 1;
                return 0;
            }
        }
    };
    let root_device = if is_root {
        followed_dev
    } else {
        root_device
    };
    let size = state.effective_size(&info.metadata, opts.apparent_size, opts.count_hard_links);
    info.size = size;
    state.statistics.add(size);
    let mut total = size;

    let descend = if is_root { info.is_dir_follow } else { info.is_real_dir };
    if !descend {
        return total;
    }
    // Pruning checks (not applied to a directory that is an expansion origin,
    // which is handled because expansion roots *are* the children; an explicit
    // aggregate root, however, is pruned when ignored / off-filesystem in the
    // multi-root walk sense. For a root the filesystem check is vacuous.)
    if !is_root || true {
        // ignore check: applies to nested dirs and to explicit roots alike.
        // (The single-input directory case never reaches here with the input
        // itself, because it is expanded before traversal.)
        if is_real_dir_ignored(path, state) {
            return total;
        }
        if opts.stay_on_filesystem && !is_root {
            if let Some(rd) = root_device {
                if info.metadata.dev() != rd {
                    return total;
                }
            }
        }
        // A root which is a symlink to a directory on another filesystem:
        // treat target device as root device (already set from followed meta).
    }
    // Collect entries first so the directory handle is closed before
    // recursing (otherwise deep trees exhaust the file-descriptor limit).
    let child_paths: Vec<PathBuf> = match fs::read_dir(path) {
        Ok(read_dir) => read_dir
            .filter_map(|e| e.ok().map(|e| e.path()))
            .collect(),
        Err(_) => Vec::new(),
    };
    for child in &child_paths {
        total += walk_aggregate(child, false, root_device, opts, state, errors);
    }
    total
}

fn is_real_dir_ignored(path: &Path, state: &TraversalState) -> bool {
    if state.ignore_set.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    // Only directories can be in the ignore set in practice; canonicalising a
    // non-existent or non-directory path simply will not match for files
    // because we only call this for directories.
    match path.canonicalize() {
        Ok(canon) => state.ignore_set.contains(&canon),
        Err(_) => state.ignore_set.contains(path),
    }
}

    fn build_root(

        nodes: &mut Vec<Node>,

        title: String,

        let id = Self::new_node(nodes, parent, name.clone(), title.clone(), fs_path.to_path_buf());
        let (_size, follow_dir, _real_dir) = self.fill_node(nodes, id, &info);
        if follow_dir {

        }
        Some(id)

    fn build_children(
        &mut self,
        nodes: &mut Vec<Node>,
        parent_id: NodeId,
        dir_path: &Path,
        root_dev: u64,
        parent_title: &str,
    ) {
        let mut entries: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
        {
            let read = match std::fs::read_dir(dir_path) { Ok(r) => r, Err(_) => return };
            for e in read { if let Ok(e) = e { entries.push(e.path()); } }
        }
        // Edge-addition order: directories (alphabetical), then other
        // non-symlink entries (alphabetical), then symlinks (in
        // directory-read order). The children list is stored reversed
        // (see below), which is the base order for stable sorting.
        let mut dirs: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
        let mut files: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
        let mut links: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
        for path in entries {
            match std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
                Ok(md) if md.file_type().is_symlink() => links.push(path),
                Ok(md) if md.file_type().is_dir() => dirs.push(path),
                _ => files.push(path),
            }

        dirs.sort_by(|a, b| a.file_name().cmp(&b.file_name()));
        files.sort_by(|a, b| a.file_name().cmp(&b.file_name()));

        }
        nodes[parent_id].children[start_len..].reverse();

            .file_name()

        Some(id)
    }
}

}

fn draw_marked_pane(buf: &mut Buffer, app: &mut App, x: usize, y: usize, w: usize, h: usize) {
    let focused = app.focus == Focus::Marked;
    let total_count: u64 = app.marked.iter().map(|&id| app.node(id).subtree_count).sum();
    let total_size: u64 = app.marked.iter().map(|&id| app.node(id).size).sum();
    let title = format!("Marked {} items ({}) ", total_count, format_size(total_size, app.format).trim_start());
    let bottom = if focused || app.marked_prompt {
        Some(" mark-toggle = space,d | remove-all = a")
    } else {
        None
    };
    // When the marked pane has been activated at least once, its bottom
    // title can remain; the simple model only shows it while focused.
    draw_block(buf, x, y, w, h, focused, &title, if focused { Some(NAV_HINT) } else { None }, bottom);
    let viewport = h.saturating_sub(2);
    // Prompt row when focused or when it has been activated via q.
    let prompt_rows = if focused || app.marked_prompt && app.focus == Focus::Main && false { 1 } else { 0 };
    let show_prompt = focused || app.marked_prompt;
    // Clamp marked selection / offset.
    let list_viewport = viewport.saturating_sub(if show_prompt { 1 } else { 0 });
    if app.marked.is_empty() {
        app.marked_selection = 0;
        app.marked_offset = 0;
    } else {
        if app.marked_selection >= app.marked.len() { app.marked_selection = app.marked.len() - 1; }
        if app.marked_selection < app.marked_offset { app.marked_offset = app.marked_selection; }
        if list_viewport > 0 && app.marked_selection >= app.marked_offset + list_viewport {
            app.marked_offset = app.marked_selection + 1 - list_viewport;
        }
        if app.marked.len() <= list_viewport { app.marked_offset = 0; }
    }
    let mut row = 0usize;
    if show_prompt {
        let yy = y + 1;
        // " Ctrl + t  to trash or  Ctrl + r  to delete without prompt"
        let mut cx = x + 1;
        let seg = |buf: &mut Buffer, cx: &mut usize, yy: usize, text: &str, style: Style, limit: usize| {
            buf.set_limit(*cx, yy, text, style, limit);
            *cx += unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width(text);
        };
        seg(buf, &mut cx, yy, " Ctrl + t ", Style::plain().fg(15).bg(0).bold(), x + w - 1);
        seg(buf, &mut cx, yy, " to trash or ", Style::plain().fg(0).bg(3).bold(), x + w - 1);
        let mut blink_style = Style::plain().fg(9).bg(0).bold();
        blink_style.blink = true;
        seg(buf, &mut cx, yy, " Ctrl + r ", blink_style, x + w - 1);
        seg(buf, &mut cx, yy, " to delete without prompt", Style::plain().fg(0).bg(3).bold(), x + w - 1);
        row += 1;
    }
    let _ = prompt_rows;
    for i in 0..list_viewport {
        let idx = app.marked_offset + i;
        if idx >= app.marked.len() { break; }
        let yy = y + 1 + row + i;
        let id = app.marked[idx];
        let node = app.node(id);
        let selected = idx == app.marked_selection && focused;
        // When unfocused, the first marked entry is still shown reversed in
        // the original when the pane was just opened? It is not; keep plain.
        let base = if selected { Style::plain().bold().reversed() } else { Style::plain() };
        if selected && w >= 3 { buf.fill(x + 1, yy, w - 3, base); }
        let name_style = Style::plain().fg(3);
        let name_style = if selected {
            let mut st = name_style;
            st.bold = true;
            st.reversed = true;
            st
        } else {
            name_style
        };
        let name_text = format!(" {}", node.name);
        let size_text = format_size(node.size, app.format);
        let size_with_space = format!("{}  ", size_text);
        let sw = unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width(size_with_space.as_str());
        if x + w - 1 > sw {
            buf.fill(x + 1, yy, (x + w - 1 - sw) - (x + 1), name_style);
        }
        let name_field_w = (x + w - 1 - sw).saturating_sub(x + 1);
        let name_target = name_field_w.saturating_sub(2);
        let name_draw = truncate_start(&name_text, name_target);
        buf.set_limit(x + 1, yy, &name_draw, name_style, x + w - 1);
        let size_style = Style::plain().fg(2);
        let size_style = if selected {
            let mut st = size_style;
            st.bold = true;
            st.reversed = true;
            st
        } else {
            size_style
        };
        if x + w - 1 > sw {
            let size_draw = format!("{} ", size_text);
            buf.set_limit(x + w - 1 - sw, yy, &size_draw, size_style, x + w - 1);
        }
    }
    if !app.marked.is_empty() {
        let cells = scrollbar_cells(list_viewport.max(1), app.marked.len(), app.marked_selection);
        for (i, is_thumb) in cells.iter().enumerate() {
            if row + i >= viewport { break; }
            buf.set(x + w - 1, y + 1 + row + i, if *is_thumb { "█" } else { "║" }, block_style(focused));
        }
    }
}

import subprocess,time,os,shutil
for n in range(21,31):
    p=f"/tmp/markn/n{n}"; shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(p)
    for i in range(n):
        open(f"{p}/f{i:02d}","wb").write(b"x"*100)
def prompt_switch(n, y=20):
    # returns smallest marked-index selection where prompt is at bottom, scanning k from last
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t","duatest"],capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","duatest","-x","80","-y",str(y),f"/tmp/origbin/executable i /tmp/markn/n{n}"])
    time.sleep(0.7)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","duatest","a"]); time.sleep(0.2)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","duatest","Tab"]); time.sleep(0.25)
    def is_bottom():
        out=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","duatest","-p"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
        for i,l in enumerate(out.splitlines()):
            if "Ctrl + t" in l: return i > (y//2)
        return None
    sel = n-1
    first_top = None
    for steps in range(n):
        b = is_bottom()
        if b is False and first_top is None:
            first_top = sel  # first (smallest) selection from top of descent where prompt is at top
            break

use crate::common::*;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;

pub struct AggregateOptions {
    pub statistics: bool,
    pub no_sort: bool,
    pub no_total: bool,
}

pub fn run(
    inputs: &[PathBuf],
    agg: &AggregateOptions,
    walk_opts: &WalkOptions,
    format: ByteFormat,
) -> anyhow::Result<i32> {
    let roots = aggregate_roots(inputs, walk_opts)?;
    let ignore_set = walk_opts.canonical_ignore_set();
    let mut state = TraversalState::new(ignore_set);
    let mut results: Vec<(u64, PathBuf, PathBuf, u64, u64)> = Vec::new(); // size, fs_path, display, errors, entries
    // A repeated directory root reports the same total as its first
    // occurrence (its file contents are counted again); this matches the
    // original, where duplicate directory inputs each show a full total
    // while duplicate hard-linked files are suppressed.
    let mut first_dir_results: std::collections::HashMap<PathBuf, (u64, u64)> =
        std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for root in &roots {
        let mut errors: u64 = 0;
        let entries_before = state.statistics.entries_traversed;
        let mut size = walk_aggregate(
            &root.fs_path,
            true,
            None,
            walk_opts,
            &mut state,
            &mut errors,
        );
        let entries = state.statistics.entries_traversed - entries_before;
        let is_dir_root = std::fs::metadata(&root.fs_path).map(|m| m.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false);
        if is_dir_root {
            if let Some(&(first_size, first_errors)) = first_dir_results.get(&root.fs_path) {
                size = first_size;
                errors = first_errors;
            } else {
                first_dir_results.insert(root.fs_path.clone(), (size, errors));
            }
        }
        results.push((size, root.fs_path.clone(), root.display.clone(), errors, entries));
    }
    if !agg.no_sort {
        // Stable sort by size ascending.
        results.sort_by_key(|r| r.0);
    }
    let stdout = std::io::stdout();
    let mut out = stdout.lock();
    let mut total_size: u64 = 0;
    let mut total_errors: u64 = 0;
    for (size, fs_path, display, errors, entries) in &results {
        total_size += size;
        total_errors += errors;
        if agg.no_sort && *errors > 0 && *entries == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        write_result(&mut out, *size, fs_path, display, *errors, format)?;
    }
    if results.len() > 1 && !agg.no_total {
        let mut line = format!(
            "\x1b[32m{}\x1b[39m total",
            format_size(total_size, format)
        );
        if total_errors > 0 {
            line.push_str(&format!(
                "  <{} IO Error{}>",
                total_errors,
                if total_errors == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
            ));
        }
        writeln!(out, "{}", line)?;
    }
    if agg.statistics {
        eprintln!(
            "Statistics {{ entries_traversed: {}, smallest_file_in_bytes: {}, largest_file_in_bytes: {} }}",
            state.statistics.entries_traversed,
            state.statistics.smallest_file_in_bytes,
            state.statistics.largest_file_in_bytes
        );
    }
    Ok(if total_errors > 0 { 1 } else { 0 })
}
